items.heading: Indian Product Hiring Has Shifted
items.text: Indian product hiring has shifted toward work samples and simulations over resumes at a large share of companies, which means these six skills are what actually gets tested in an interview loop, not what gets listed on a certificate.

rows: Flipkart, Google, and a small set of large product companies run defined, mentored APM tracks with rotations.
Often campus-hiring only or a narrow annual application window; high competition for a small number of seats.
Product companies that also hire APMs off-cycle
Amazon, Razorpay, Swiggy, Zoho, Freshworks, PhonePe, and many funded startups hire junior PMs outside a formal APM brand name.
Less structured mentorship than a named program, but a real door if you missed the campus window.
Consulting and analytics-heavy firms sometimes move strong analysts into product-adjacent or full PM roles internally.
Slower and less visible than a direct APM hire, but a legitimate side door if you are already inside a large organisation.

visuals.heading: Own One Thing End

items.heading: Own One Thing End
items.text: Own one thing end-to-end wherever you already are: a feature, a process gap, or a small internal tool nobody has claimed.

items.heading: Write IT Up the Way
items.text: Write it up the way a PM would, the problem, the options you considered, the trade-off you picked, and the measured result, not the way an engineer, designer, or analyst would.

items.heading: Build or Improve One Small
items.text: Build or improve one small thing outside work if your current role gives you no real ownership. It does not need to make money; it needs a clear problem, a decision, and a way to explain what you would measure to know it worked.

items.heading: Get One Honest Outside Opinion
items.text: Get one honest outside opinion from someone already working in product before you spend months applying on the strength of a case study nobody else has stress-tested.
